item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Sweden is starting to feel the impact of the war in Iran, Moderate youth leader confident of solution for Sweden's teen deportations, and three wolverine cubs born at Kolmården Zoo. Here's the latest news.

item.title: SKARS-GUIDE: Who's who in Sweden's Skarsgård acting dynasty?
item.description: Alongside Abba and Ikea, Oscar nominee Stellan Skarsgård and his many children are some of Sweden's most famous international exports. But who are they and what have you seen them in?

item.title: 'Sweden is setting itself up for a losing battle' on skilled immigration
item.description: This week’s episode of Sweden in Focus Extra features an interview with Patrick Gallen, spokesperson for Fair Transition.

item.title: NEW: The Local’s self-paced Swedish course
item.description: Due to popular demand The Local's self-paced online Swedish course for beginners is back, designed to make learning flexible and practical.

item.title: How to get your Swedish tax rebate in April
item.description: March 31st is your last chance to declare if you want to get any money you're owed by the Swedish Tax Agency next month.

item.title: Sweden's 2026 tax season officially under way
item.description: The Swedish Tax Agency has started sending out tax declarations for everybody with a digital postbox. What should you be aware of when declaring?

item.title: Swedes told to keep 1,000 kronor in cash at home in case of crisis or war
item.description: Do you have enough cash at home to see you through a week of cards not working? The Riksbank has issued new guidelines for how Sweden's extremely digitised society can cope if payment systems shut down.

item.title: Politics in Sweden: Sweden needs to get off the fence on Iran – but how?
item.description: The US and Israel’s lightning attack on Iran has left Sweden with a dilemma. As Nato’s newest member with a large Iranian community – but also a traditional stickler for international law – Sweden has so far chosen to sit on the fence in the conflict. The question is how long that can be sustained, writes The Local's James Savage.

item.title: Swedish games boss warns 'retroactive' citizenship reforms 'not good for industry'
item.description: Pushing through citizenship reforms without transitional rules will make Sweden less attractive to international talent, the acting head of the Swedish Games Industry Association has warned.

item.title: Swedish Fika Calendar: Why Swedes eat cake on the first Thursday of March
item.description: Hej and welcome to the latest instalment of The Local's Fika Calender, where we guide you through the most important cake, pastry and other food-related days in the Swedish year.
